### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**9** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-record-context/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-record-context/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b0536e12b1d58e720b883582644c8eec07deb887` — the merge of head `2831c87e9ec67f2993ca9acf63240ed34e069b0d` into base `93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b0536e12b1d58e720b883582644c8eec07deb887 && git checkout b0536e12b1d58e720b883582644c8eec07deb887
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f 2831c87e9ec67f2993ca9acf63240ed34e069b0d && git checkout -B drift-repro 93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f && git merge --no-ff 2831c87e9ec67f2993ca9acf63240ed34e069b0d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93bd45957bc4a43eb54d8fec2b36f1cbef41dc5f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2831c87e9ec67f2993ca9acf63240ed34e069b0d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/record-context-tools.zod.ts + packages/services/service-record-context/src/body-outline.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/record-context-tools.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/sentences.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/index.ts

Inputs read: card #37178 with every comment (the triage notes, the implementation claim 7152342456, the dev report 7153677982), PR #37222's body, file list and net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on the head. The review claim is PR comment 7153710557. The rest of the diff (the two test files, the changeset, the generated reference page) is the lane seat's ACCEPT; the changeset and the reference page were read only to judge ② and the declarations.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Published output enum `RecordContextNoteKind` gains `outline_truncated`: right, and a pure widening in this tree.** Every reader of the enum at the head is the spec module itself and the executor that writes the notes. No file in the repository switches over the kinds, exhaustively or otherwise. The MCP door registers `get_record_context` with a description and an input schema only (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`, the `registerTool` call beside `get_record`): it declares no output schema and returns the executor's answer as text, so no transport validates a note's kind and none refuses an unknown one. The runtime and stdio bridges pass the answer through. The only parse of an answer against `GetRecordContextOutputSchema` is the service's own test, against the same head. The one consumer class a new output value can break is one compiled against an older spec that parses the answer strictly or switches exhaustively; none exists in the tree, and the changeset says so in words ("a consumer that switches over note kinds exhaustively must handle the new value").
- **`RecordContextBody.outline`'s description changes, its shape does not: right.** The accept-set of the field is unchanged; the sentence added states the bound and names the note.
- **`@objectstack/service-record-context` gains the export `RECORD_CONTEXT_OUTLINE_MAX_ENTRIES`: right.** An added export beside `RECORD_CONTEXT_BODY_MAX_CHARS`; nothing is removed or renamed. `boundedOutline` and `BodyOutlineEntry` stay internal to the package, which matches the index.
- **Behaviour of `get_record_context` narrows for one input class: right, and stated.** A long body with more than 80 headings, or whose listing would pass 8000 serialized characters, used to list every heading and now lists a subset with a note. That is the card's ask. A second class changes too: a long body whose first-admitted heading cannot be listed used to answer with an outline and now answers with truncated text and `body_truncated`. Both are output changes of a tool, not of anything an author writes.
- **Generated faces follow.** The reference page carries the new enum value and the new description in both tables; `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Spec property liveness` and `Build Docs` are success on the head.
- **Gate verdicts on the head:** 60 success, 10 skipped, 0 failure. `Test Core` (10 of 10 shards), `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `PR-body guards` are success. The skipped runs are path-selected or queue-only (`Lint UI`, the Dogfood shard matrix, the opt-in harnesses).

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: one value is added to a published output enum, and nothing is taken away. The line is present, line-initial, in both the PR body and the changeset body.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no key, accepted value or metadata type an author can write changes. `RecordContextNote` is tool output; `ai_context` packs are untouched.
- `patch` on `@objectstack/spec` and on `@objectstack/service-record-context` is right under AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3: the level follows the metadata-protocol kind alone, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. Both packages the diff moves are named. No BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition are owed, because nothing an author or a consumer could write is removed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` in the dev report is empty. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, "the outline's `.describe()` and the new kind's docblock are spec prose in the claimed file": answered. Both sentences were read against the executor and hold (④).
- Dev flag, the tests went into the two existing test files and not into a card-named file as the claim's file surface said: the reason given is the shared-harness rule in AGENTS.md. This is outside ④ and is the lane seat's to accept.
- Dev decision, a new note kind instead of the existing `truncated` mark plus `body_truncated`: answered, right. `RecordContextBody.truncated` is published as "present when `text` was cut", and an outline answer has no `text`; `body_truncated` is published as a character cut of text. Reusing either would change a published meaning without a visible change. The claim asked for this to be measured and it was.
- Dev decision, a character bound beside the entry cap: answered, right, and required by the card's acceptance. A heading and the anchor derived from it are as long as the author makes them, so an entry cap alone bounds nothing.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no read, no id materialisation and no in-app join. `boundedOutline` works on the body string the root read already returned.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/ai/record-context-tools.zod.ts`, against ADR-0160 D3 on `main` and its first consumer, the executor.**

- The enum value and its docblock agree with the executor: `outline_truncated` is pushed only in the outline branch, only when `omitted` is above zero, exactly once, right after `body_outline`. "Its sentence says how many headings are not listed" is true in both languages. "Every heading's anchor still reads its section" is true: see the executor below.
- The `outline` description, "a cut leaves out the deepest headings first and is stated by an `outline_truncated` note", holds. Admission is in (level, body order) and stops at the first heading that does not fit, so no listed heading is deeper than any omitted one.
- Agreement with ADR-0160 D3. D3 says a longer body is carried as an outline, that every cut is stated in the notes, that a note is a fixed sentence of the executor's in the caller's locale and never carries record text, and that bounds are constants of the service pinned by test with no number set by the record. The change holds to each: the cut has a note, the note takes only the body field's name (a name the caller's served schema shows, since this branch runs only for a body that is neither hidden nor withheld) and three counts, the cap is a service constant, and the lane's tests pin it at 80. The cut carries no structural mark on `body`; D3 allows a mark and does not require one, and the note's `kind` is the machine-readable carrier. Nothing in D3 is reversed, so AGENTS.md Prime Directive 13 is not engaged.

**`body-outline.ts`.**

- The bound is exact. `chars` starts at 2 for the brackets and each admitted entry adds its `JSON.stringify` length plus one comma after the first, so `chars` equals `JSON.stringify(outline).length` at every step, and an entry is admitted only while that stays at or below `RECORD_CONTEXT_BODY_MAX_CHARS`. The entry cap is tested before each admission, so at most 80 are listed. Both bounds hold whatever the body holds, which is the card's acceptance.
- 80 is consistent with the character bound: at the measured mean of about 95 characters an entry, 80 entries is about 7600 characters, so on ordinary documents the entry cap binds first and the character bound is the backstop for long headings.
- Selection is right. The sort is by level then by original index (an explicit tie-break, so it does not rely on sort stability); the admitted set is re-sorted by index, so the listing is in body order. `omitted` is `headings.length` minus the admitted count.
- Anchors are untouched: `boundedOutline` copies the anchor `headingsOf` gave, and `headingsOf` de-duplicates slugs over every heading before any cut, so a listed anchor is the same cut or not.
- Cost: one sort of the headings and at most 81 `JSON.stringify` calls; the reader's linear-scan property is not affected in practice.

**`record-context-tools.ts`.**

- A section call resolves its anchor with `sectionOf(text, headings, args.anchor)` over the full `headings` array; `boundedOutline` runs only when no anchor was given and the body is past the bound. So an anchor past the cap reads its section, as the docblock and the changeset say.
- The note's arithmetic is exact: listed is `listed.outline.length`, total is `headings.length`, and the sentence computes the remainder as total minus listed, which equals `omitted`.
- The fallback is stated, never silent: when nothing can be listed the body is carried to the bound with `truncated` and `body_truncated`. An empty outline is never returned.

**`sentences.ts`.** `outlineTruncated` exists in `en` and `zh-Hans` with the same three values, and the `satisfies` clause plus the union return type make a missing language a type error (`TypeScript Type Check` is success). The picker maps `zh-CN` to `zh-Hans`. Neither sentence can carry record text.

**`index.ts`.** Exports the new constant beside the body bound. Agrees with the changeset.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):

- nit — "Serialized" means compact JSON. The MCP door renders the answer with a two-space indent (`jsonText` in `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`), which adds about 54 characters an entry, so a full outline is up to about 12,300 characters on that wire. The answer is still bounded by the two constants, and the body bound is likewise counted before serialization, so the acceptance holds. The jsdoc on `boundedOutline` could say "compact JSON". Accepted deviation.
- nit — The English and Chinese sentences end with "a listed section's text includes the headings under it". That is true, and it helps when deeper headings are cut. In a flat cut (the card's own case: 300 headings at one level) the 220 unlisted headings are under no listed section, and the sentence may lead a model to think the listed sections cover them. The first half of the note does say they are not listed, and their anchors do resolve, but the outline gives a caller no way to learn those anchors. A sentence that says sections under no listed heading are not reachable from this outline, or a paged outline, is a follow-up card; it is not this card's ask.
- nit — The character bound uses `break`, so one over-long heading stops admission of everything after it in (level, body order). When that heading is the first admitted, a body with many short, listable headings falls back to truncated text. That needs a single heading of about 4000 characters, the outcome is stated by `body_truncated`, and it keeps the "nothing deeper than an omitted heading is listed" property, so the choice is defensible. It does make two published sentences slightly narrow: `RecordContextBody.truncated` still lists "a long body with no headings" as the whole-body case, and ADR-0160 D3 says the same. Follow-up: add "or none short enough to list" where those are next edited.
- nit — The changeset says "a body whose only heading is too long to list"; the code's condition is the first-admitted heading, whatever else the body holds. Fixable on the prose face.
- nit — ADR-0160 D3's body paragraph names two constants (the body bound and the related-row cap) and three kinds of cut. The outline cap is a third constant and a fourth cut, in the spirit of the paragraph but not in its text. A one-line amendment is a follow-up on that governed surface.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37178-outline-entry-cap`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgv2LZN1W2qSYTZvYs`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · repo:objectstack#3 · head 2831c87e · 2026-11-25T05:28Z

Head-sha: `2831c87e9ec67f2993ca9acf63240ed34e069b0d`

No must-fix, no should-fix. The L2 at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on this head is PASS with nothing open: comment 7153800496, claim 7153710557. This is Tier S: no governed path, 247 changed lines on this card's only PR. `needs:contract-review` is not owed, because a same-head PASS is on record. ai-A lands it after ACCEPT and green.

### Read and found right (head 2831c87e)

- **`l1-face --pr 37222`:** 13 items clean.
  - Draft, base `main`. `Fixes #37178` binds only this card.
  - The declarations are `Clause-②: yes (widening)` · `Metadata-protocol: none`.
  - The changeset names both published packages moved (spec, service-record-context). `patch` is right for a non-protocol widening (AGENTS.md). The L2 found no exhaustive switch over `RecordContextNoteKind` in the tree, and no output schema on the MCP door that would refuse the new kind.
  - 60 success, 10 expected skips, 0 failed. `mergeable_state` clean.
- **`Fixes` is right.** The card asks for the outline's entries to be capped by a service constant. `RECORD_CONTEXT_OUTLINE_MAX_ENTRIES` (80) is exported and pinned. The listing also stays within `RECORD_CONTEXT_BODY_MAX_CHARS`. A cut is stated by one `outline_truncated` note with exact listed, total and omitted counts, in en and zh-Hans. Anchors past the cap still read their section.
- **Changeset and the generated `record-context-tools.mdx`, sentence by sentence.** The cap, the character bound, "shallowest levels first … in body order", "every heading's `anchor` still reads its section", the new note kind and the consumer warning all hold. The one exception is the "only heading" sentence (L2 nit 4: the code's condition is the first-admitted heading). The mdx rows are the spec `.describe()` text and the enum list, regenerated.
- The tests landed in the two existing test files, per the shared-harness rule.

### Accepted deviations (nits from the L2; each needs a follow-up card under the nit rule, or a prose-face fix)

- **N2, the one to file first.** In a flat cut (every heading at one level, as in the card's own 300-heading case), the omitted headings sit under no listed section. The answer then gives no way to learn their anchors, so those sections cannot be reached through the tool. The note's sentence "a listed section's text includes the headings under it" misleads there. The follow-up should decide how an omitted section is reached, for example a continuation or an offset on the outline, and fix the sentence.
- **N1.** The bound is on compact JSON. The MCP door pretty-prints, so a full outline is up to about 12,300 characters on the wire. That is still bounded by the constants.
- **N3.** One very long first-admitted heading drops the whole outline to truncated text, though other headings could be listed. It is stated by `body_truncated`.
- **N4.** The changeset's "only heading" wording. It can be fixed on the prose face.
- **N5.** ADR-0160 D3 does not yet name the outline cap as a further constant and cut. That needs a one-line amendment, which is a governed follow-up.

### Landing to-do

`Fixes #37178` closes the card on merge. File the N2 card, and carry N5 to the next ADR-0160 amendment.
